chapter_title: The Chapter of the Name of the Fathers
spiritual_reading:
The first Divine Principle, as it is first received and made present, is acknowledged as the originating Love in its unmeasured power. That power is the whole ultimate plane in which this Love is made stable for operation, and within that plane the pure being of wisdom that shines from it and surrounds every abundance of goods and truths, together with all angelic states and all ordered communities of reception, is set in governance.

Also, the mediating Divine that goes forth as the third in the order of manifestation is acknowledged as an originating source, because through it Love is carried into fixed presentation. Its unmeasured power is the living union of love and wisdom in their active conveyance, within which it dwells and by which it is established.

Again, the Divine Human made manifest as saving wisdom is likewise acknowledged as an originating source, because through it truth becomes living and restorative in the lower degrees. Its unmeasured power is the living conveyance of truth from love, within which it dwells and by which it is established.

fills.fill: as the great earth, and his root is in it; and
fills.notes: The Father’s ‘greatness’ is the ultimate plane of establishment (earth). Correspondentially, ‘root’ expresses first fixation and stability in ultimates (Love made present and operative). The clause prepares the shift from the plane (earth) to what proceeds within it (the light-essence that swathes and governs).

fills.fill: of this greatness; and the boundary of the light
fills.notes: The text moves from the Father’s established plane (great earth) to the proceeding wisdom-light that surrounds (‘swathes’) goods and truths (‘rich gods’), angelic states, and ordered abodes (‘dwellings’). Calling this light the ‘boundary’ matches the spiritual sense: the irradiating wisdom that encompasses and defines the whole abundance, and therefore can be said to be ‘set over it’ in governance.

assessment: Both lacunae are restorably constrained by the correspondential structure: (1) a clause must complete the idea of stability of the Father in the ‘earth’ by a fixation term (‘root’), and (2) a genitive bridge must connect ‘dwellings’ to ‘is set over it’ by naming the encompassing wisdom-light as the delimiting boundary of the Father’s greatness. Exact wording is not fully determinable, but the demanded concepts are tight.
